# Professor Tim Legrand

> Professor of International Security in the Department of Politics and International Relations at Adelaide University, and Australian Research Council Future Fellow (2025-2029). He researches blacklisting and sanctions, the proscription of terrorist organisations, counter-terrorism, transgovernmental policy networks and digital security.

- Website: https://silegrand.github.io/timlegrand/
- Institutional profile: https://researchers.adelaide.edu.au/profile/tim.legrand
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5205-5914
- Email: tim.legrand@adelaide.edu.au
- Last updated: 2026-11-12

## Current roles

- Professor of International Security: Department of Politics and International Relations, Adelaide University
- ARC Future Fellow: Australian Research Council, 2025–2029
- Editor-in-Chief: Australian Journal of International Affairs, since 2023, with Professor Joanne Wallis
- Associate Dean (Research Performance): Faculty of Arts, Business, Law and Economics, since 2022
- Board Member, Executive Committee: Australian Institute of International Affairs, since 2023
- Associate Editor: Global Perspectives, University of California Press, since 2020
- Board Member: Palgrave Macmillan Series in Political Economy, since 2020
- Associate Editor: Criminology and Criminal Justice, since 2016
- Adjunct Associate Professor of Public Policy: Centre for Governance and Policy Analysis, University of Canberra, since 2015
- Co-Convenor: Australian Political Studies Association Policy Studies Research Group

## Background

- Joined the Department of Politics and International Relations at the University of Adelaide in July 2018. The institution is now Adelaide University.
- Research and lecturing posts: National Security College, Australian National University
- Research and lecturing posts: ARC Centre of Excellence in Policing and Security, Griffith University
- Secretary-Treasurer: Australian Political Studies Association
- Visiting research fellowships: Sciences Po Paris, Johns Hopkins University, University of East Anglia and Stockholm University
- Policy roles in UK government: Home Office, Department of Health and Department for Communities and Local Government
- PhD in Political Science: University of Birmingham, 2008. Funded by the Economic and Social Research Council

## Research strands

- Blacklisting and sanctions: How states designate people and organisations as threats, restricting their movement, money and freedoms, and how the same instruments are turned on dissenters and minorities.
- Proscription and counter-terrorism: The law, politics and symbolism of banning terrorist organisations, from Westminster debates to proscription regimes in Cameroon, Nigeria, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
- Transgovernmental networks and policy transfer: The elite networks of officials through which Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and the US share intelligence, doctrine and policy ideas, largely out of public view.
- Digital security and liberal democracy: Foreign interference, online pathways to violent extremism and the governance of cyber security across the Anglosphere.

## Funded projects

- 2025–2029. New approaches to combat the misuse of blacklists as tools of repression. Australian Research Council, Future Fellowship. FT240100855.
- 2024–2026. Digital pathways to violent extremism in young Australians: intelligence imperatives and implications. Australian Research Council, National Intelligence and Security Discovery. With Dr Nathan Manning and Dr Melissa-Ellen Dowling.
- 2020–2023. The Proscription of Terrorist Organisations in Illiberal States. Australian Research Council, Discovery Project. DP200102447. With Professor Lee Jarvis, University of East Anglia. Case studies in Cameroon, Nigeria, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
- 2021. Countering Foreign Interference. Department of Defence.
- 2021. Modelling Social Influence in Wargame Setting. Department of Defence, ORNet. With Dr Mehwish Nasim, Flinders University.
- 2020. Cyber Security in the Anglosphere. Cyber Security Cooperative Research Centre. With Dr Nikola Pijovic.
- 2018. Tackling Transnational Threats: The Architecture of Anglosphere Security Collaboration. Gerda Henkel Stiftung, Special Programme Security, Society and the State. AZ 09/KF/18.
- 2017. Power, public policy and boundary-making. Australian Political Studies Association, Workshop Grant. With P. Fawcett, J. Lewis and S. O’Sullivan.
- 2016. Governance of cyber security. Macquarie Telecom.

Tim has secured more than $2 million in Australian Research Council grants.

## Policy engagement

- Advises the United Nations on blacklisting and sanctions in East Africa and Afghanistan.
- Research cited at the International Court of Justice in The Hague.
- Consults on blacklisting and sanctions compliance for UNDP in Afghanistan, the Swiss Refugee Council and World Vision.
- Works with the Department of Defence and the Department of Home Affairs on protecting liberal democracy from digital threats.
- Research has supported training for the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Home Affairs, Defence, the Australian Federal Police and the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.
- Appointed expert advisor to the Commonwealth Inspector of Transport Security on aviation and maritime security in 2016.
- Work has formed the basis of submissions to a Queensland Parliamentary committee, the COAG Review of Counter-Terrorism Legislation and the Commonwealth Independent National Security Legislation Monitor.
- Has delivered public policy training to federal officials in Canberra and to government officials from Bhutan, Indonesia, Mexico, South Korea and Vietnam.
